description: Mechanics-15, 2D: the 15 ogbench M7-M10 mazes (every non-empty combination of portals, death, rotating and frozen tiles on the 18x18 dense kr/sg/kb skeleton) on Kimi K3, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The R1 fixed cell (minimal/image_only/egocentric/zero_shot/stateless, step_by_step, progress_stall_k=30) with context_window=full instead of text_summary_and_last_n. MiniGrid backend (no render block); the same manifest serves the NL and 3D runs through run_config.mechanics_15_nl.json and run_config.mechanics_15_3d.json.
_note_no_conditions: No conditions key => single (default) cell built from experiment_config overlay. Do NOT add conditions (that would re-enable the sweep).
_note_requires: context_window=full comes from PR #54 (R2 full context). Launching before it is on the launched SHA fails at config load.
_note_model_params: Equal 64k output caps (max_tokens; max_completion_tokens for OpenAI and Kimi K3). Thinking on for all three. Opus 5.5: effort=xhigh, no sampling params, Message Batches API via the lockstep worker (worker_role=lockstep-worker; coordinator STALE_AFTER_SECONDS >= 12600). Kimi K3: always thinks, reasoning_effort=max (Moonshot's default, set explicitly for provenance), no thinking object or sampling params; plain worker on the sync API (Moonshot Batch support for kimi-k3 unverified). GPT-6 Astra: reasoning_effort=xhigh, flex tier, image_detail=high, plain worker (the OpenAI agent has no batch path), spend_cap_usd=160 is a per-process hard stop on the Astra worker's running total (see _note_cost for where it stops the run; pair it with an OpenAI project budget). context_window=full resends every prior decision frame each query (history capped by max_history_tokens), so per-episode input grows quadratically with steps: estimate cost before launch.
_note_cost: Projection for the 15 mazes with caching on, per model. Episode length is the main unknown. One query is one action; the 15 mazes need 49-161 actions on their BFS shortest path (102 on average, 1,532 in all) and are capped at 3x that (147-483, 306 on average). An episode ends earlier on death, or after progress_stall_k=30 steps without reaching a new state. Query i of an N-query episode reads the i-1 earlier steps from cache, writes the newest step and sends a tail uncached, so an episode's input is s*N(N-1)/2*read + s*N*write + t*N*input; output is o*N*output. Summed maze by maze: it grows with N^2, so long episodes dominate. Inputs: Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3 s = 477 tokens per history step, t = ~548 (count_tokens on M10; a smoke request holding 483 576x576 frames, M10's step cap, measured ~470 per frame and both providers accepted it); GPT-6 Astra s = ~399, t = ~500 (measured on M10, image_detail=high). Output per query was measured on r1_S4_10x10_dense_1, the only maze run as full episodes: Opus 5.5 xhigh ~450, Kimi K3 max ~10.5k (median latency 314 s), Astra xhigh ~220. Prices per 1M tokens (input / cache read / 1h cache write / output): Opus 5.5 batch $2 / $0.20 / $4 / $10; Kimi K3 $3 / $0.30 / $6 / $15; Astra flex $5 / $0.50 / $6.25 / $25. Total (input + output) over the 15 mazes if every episode runs 1x / 1.5x / 2x / 3x (the step cap) its shortest path: Opus 5.5 ~$20 / ~$36 / ~$56 / ~$108; Kimi K3 ~$260 / ~$400 / ~$546 / ~$855; Astra ~$33 / ~$63 / ~$101 / ~$203; panel ~$313 / ~$498 / ~$702 / ~$1,167. Kimi K3's output alone is 62-77% of the panel total, and its ~10.5k tokens per query come from a 10x10 maze; these 18x18 mechanics mazes may think longer. Uncached input would be 6-9x the cached input (Opus 5.5 ~$85 / ~$189 / ~$334 / ~$749 instead of ~$13 / ~$25 / ~$42 / ~$88). Cached figures assume every query hits; a miss rewrites the whole prefix. Astra's spend_cap_usd=160 is a running total for the one Astra worker process, which runs all 15 mazes: with caching it stops the worker only if episodes average about 2.6x their shortest path; uncached it would stop at about 1x. Calibrate on M10 (run_config.mechanics_15_2d_calib.json) and re-project from its measured episode lengths and output tokens before launch.
_note_launch: Launch with difficulty_max_static_score = 8000 (--difficulty-max-static-score 8000, fleet DIFFICULTY_MAX=8000), set for this panel: the largest static score is M10's, about 7,840. Stage 2 refuses the run if any selected maze scores above the cap. Stage 2 takes tens of minutes per maze on these 18x18 mechanics mazes: pre-score with a local coordinator-prepare and launch with PRESCORED_TASKS. Serve the coordinator with STALE_AFTER_SECONDS >= 12600 for the lockstep Opus group.
_note_cache: Prompt caching on (PRs #64/#65): experiment_config.prompt_cache=true with context_window=full marks the newest history step and the previous request's newest step, so each query reads the system prompt and every earlier frame, inventory and action from cache and writes only the new step; the current frame, budget/stall lines and question sit after the last breakpoint. Measured 2026-10-21 on r1_S4_10x10_dense_1 (31 queries, caching on): Opus 5.5 read 85% of its input from cache on both the sync and the lockstep batch path (92-93% by the last query, each query reading exactly what the previous one wrote); Kimi K3 read 89% over 25 queries. Opus: the fleet run uses Message Batches with batch_cache_ttl=1h (the default; R1 lockstep rounds p50 7 min, p90 42 min, 2.4% over 1 h); a local run uses the sync API with cache_ttl=5m (the default; measured sync latencies 3-61 s). GPT-6 Astra: enable_prompt_cache=true selects explicit breakpoints. Measured 2026-10-21 on M10 (queries 10 and 11, flex, image_detail=high): with it on, query 11 read 4,224 of its 4,490 input tokens from cache; with it off (OpenAI's implicit mode), both queries read 0. On r1_S4_10x10_dense_1 (31 queries, solved) Astra read 76% of its input from cache (83% by the last query): OpenAI caches only prompts of 1,024+ tokens, so that 10x10 maze's first 9 queries read nothing, and reads (in 128-token blocks) sometimes lagged a few steps behind the newest breakpoint. Kimi K3: implicit prefix cache with prompt_cache_ttl=1h. The 5m tier still hit with start-to-start query gaps up to 8.9 min in the R1 rerun, but K3's latency is erratic (max-effort queries up to ~9 min), so 1h guards against misses for about +10% on K3 input ($6/M vs $3/M writes).
